products.description: About the Author R.T. Donlon spends his mornings with coffee in hand and computer open to his next novel in progress. He is a high school teacher by day, a basketball coach by night, and an author everywhere in between. He is the author of a zombie-tale thriller called Walls, a supernatural fantasy novel called The Reaper Trials, and now, a 12-part fantasy epic called The Edge of a New Beginning: Book 1 of the City of Shadow & Dust Series. R.T. Donlon is fascinated by the idea of humanity transcending the impossible. Corrupt kings, angry gods, zombie-killing gunmen, mysterious monsters, and vengeful demons are just some of the characters that fill the pages of his work, but the focal ones are human-real, unmitigated humans. It is in those characters where the true story lies. Science fiction and fantasy may be born in the imagination, but it's the characters that make them real.

products.title: The Transall Saga
products.description: Review Gary Paulsen, bestselling author of Brian's Winter , brings us a new dimension in adventure with The Transall Saga . * "[A] world of rare charm, a captivating, well-realized realm, where fantastical elements force the protagonist to discover and employ the greatest strengths of his humanity."-- Booklist, starred About the Author Gary Paulsen is the distinguished author of many critically acclaimed books for young people, His most recent books are Lawn Boy Returns , Woods Runner , Notes from the Dog , Mudshark , Lawn Boy , Molly McGinty Has a Really Good Day , The Time Hackers , and The Amazing Life of Birds (The Twenty Day Puberty Journal of Duane Homer Leech) . Excerpt. © Reprinted by permission. All rights reserved. A snorting sound came from beyond the trees.  A large hairy animal resembling a buffalo charged into the small opening.  It had long tusks, beady eyes and a piglike snout.  The thing waved its shaggy head back and forth, sniffed the air and bellowed. This can't be happening. Mark edged toward the nearest tree.  The instant he moved, the beast spotted him.  It pawed the ground with its large hooves and lowered its massive head to attack.There was no time to think.  Mark jumped for the closest branch and swung up into the tree just as the sharp tusks rushed underneath him.  The animal stopped and sniffed the air again.  Unable to locate its victim, the creature snorted and ambled off into the red forest.Mark stayed on the branch.  He was shaking and his mind was in a whirl.  "All right.  Would a hallucination attack me? This must be a real place," he whispered.  "But where is it? And how did I get here?"He thought back to the night before and the energy-charged light. It has to be.  Whatever that blue light was, it's the key.  When I fell into the tube it transported me to . . . to where? I don't even know if I'm on Earth anymore. Read more

dialogue.user:
Thanks for the suggestions! A couple of these look promising. I’d like to know a bit more about "The Odd Profession of Jeremy Scratch" and "The Transall Saga." 

Could you tell me if either of them has any philosophical themes or educational elements? And is the writing style in either book more thought-provoking or more action-focused?
dialogue.agent:
Here’s a summary of both books with attention to your questions:

- "The Odd Profession of Jeremy Scratch" ($5.84, 4.8/5): This book has strong philosophical themes. The protagonist, a professor and assassin of serial killers, navigates moral complexity and questions of good versus evil, global racism, and the preservation of humanity. The narrative reaches a philosophical crossroads about justice and humanity’s future. Reviews describe the story as fast-paced with many twists, combining thought-provoking elements with action. The writing is described as compelling and unique, with a focus on purpose, motivation, and turbulent relationships.

- "The Transall Saga" ($7.99, 4.7/5): This is an adventure-focused survival story about a boy transported to an unknown world. There are some educational and philosophical undertones—such as discovering inner strength, adapting to new societies, and moral growth. Reviewers highlight the protagonist’s journey of self-discovery and building human bonds, but the book is more centered on adventure and action than deep philosophical inquiry.

If you’re looking for the most thought-provoking and philosophical, "The Odd Profession of Jeremy Scratch" fits best. For a more action-oriented adventure with some underlying themes of growth and adaptation, "The Transall Saga" is strong. Would you like more reviews or details for either title?

result.title: The Odd Profession of Jeremy Scratch
result.features: Professor Jeremy Scratch is a human taxidermist … and an assassin of serial killers. The Odd Profession of Jeremy Scratch is a slipstream story that crosses over and under conventional spy fiction genre edges. That’s because his closest friend in college, Professor Tunji Farabi, is an African revolutionist who is also the Chair of African American Studies at NYU. Both men see themselves as being on good and honorable missions. Their personal visions, however, are not viewed through the same glasses. Farabi’s organization, SAGE, kills innocent people in many different countries on five continents. The professors deal with different issues: death and dying, worldwide racism, and human preservation. They arrive at a philosophical crossroads and the question the reader will ponder is how strange are their worlds and is what they are doing ultimately good … Together the utopian and dystopian endings may be remarkably just, hopeful, and human.

result.title: The Transall Saga
result.features: Mark's solo camping trip in the desert turns into a terrifying and thrilling odyssey when a mysterious beam of light transports him to another time on what appears to be another planet. As Mark searches for a pathway back to his own time on Earth, he must make a new life in a new world. His encounters with primitive tribes bring the joy of human bonds, but violence and war as well--and, finally, a contest in which he discovers his own startling powers.

top_reviews.title: Twists and Turns
top_reviews.text:
I enjoyed the read. It was compelling. The story was poignant. Along the way, you experience the protagonist fighting for what he believes in., Jeremy Scratch does it in what is his turbulent world. Not much different from our current climate.
Doors open for some people and they talk about it. Others like Scratch walk through doors as if it is what's supposed to happen. He even walks through doors that you or I would walk away.
Scratch’s life force is his Chi. His Chi allows him to flow to deal with the obstacles during the journey.
His old friend Tunji from Africa, weaves in and out of the story. He is fighting for his own cause. Is he a friend or an enemy? If he is a friend, can their friendship withstand the turbulence? And who is Dada? Who is she?
You experience the story as it twists and turns its way through the fast-paced complex life of Jeremy Scratch. This means diamonds, caskets, and felons.
Scratch is a criminal, crusader, entrepreneur, or a little of each.
Scratch and Dada travel the world of excitement. As the story comes together tension builds to an unexpected explosive climax.

top_reviews.title: Hang on to your seat!
top_reviews.text: This story is unique and easily understood. It's odd in it's own sense ... Does a taxidermist work on his own killings? Does he stuff the human bodies himself? The story is pretty awesome ☺️. I liked it a lot!

top_reviews.title: INTRIGUING!
top_reviews.text: Having only read the prologue and on that alone this book is a definite 5 star.  The author's ability to entice readers with his wordsmithing alone is amazing...I'm intrigued by the Silk Road, buying dead bodies;, going back to Poland and feeling the DANGER!  This is 1976!

dialogue.user: That’s really helpful, thank you! "The Odd Profession of Jeremy Scratch" sounds like it has some of the deeper philosophical content I’m interested in, while still fitting my budget. Before I decide, could you tell me whether the writing and themes in "The Odd Profession of Jeremy Scratch" are generally accessible, or do reviewers mention it being difficult to follow? Also, is there anything about its educational value beyond just being thought-provoking—for instance, does it explore psychological or social topics in depth?
dialogue.agent:
Reviewers for "The Odd Profession of Jeremy Scratch" note that the story is unique, compelling, and easily understood. The writing style is described as accessible, with the author’s “wordsmithing” making the story engaging without being difficult to follow. One review specifically mentions how the narrative draws readers in and maintains interest through twists and clear prose.

As for educational value, the book goes beyond philosophical musing—it explores psychological themes (e.g., the protagonist’s motives, Chi, and moral struggles), as well as social issues like worldwide racism, friendship, and what defines justice in turbulent times. The plot involves international perspectives and the ethical tensions between different worldviews, including activism and revolution. Readers reflect on both the personal and broader societal impacts of the characters’ choices.

If you want a book that balances accessibility, psychological depth, and contemporary social themes, "The Odd Profession of Jeremy Scratch" looks well suited to your interests. Would you like to proceed with this one, or do you want to know more about any other titles?
